title: Coroners inquest into death of man in Ridge RCMP custody
article: The B.C. Coroners Service is conducting an inquest into the death of a 54-year-old Maple Ridge man.

Ian Alexander Young was taken into police custody on Oct. 17, 2008 after paramedics found him lying on the side of the road intoxicated. Several hours later, during regular cell checks at Ridge Meadows RCMP detachment, officers found the man breathing, but non-responsive, RCMP Cpl. Dale Carr said at the time.

Young was transported to Ridge Meadows Hospital, where doctors determined he needed medical intervention. The man was rushed to Royal Columbian Hospital, where he underwent surgery. Carr said the surgery was to repair an "internal injury that was pre-existing prior to having contact with police."
Young died two days later in hospital.

The coroner's inquest is scheduled for Aug. 10-13 at the coroners courthouse in Burnaby. Presiding coroner Vincent Stancato and a jury will publicly hear evidence from subpoenaed witnesses in order to determine the facts surrounding the death. The jury will have the opportunity to make recommendations aimed at preventing deaths under similar circumstances in the future.
The inquest is a fact-finding process that can't make any finding have legal consequence.
